'''Kahlil (Kay) Ameer Felder, Jr.''' (born March 29, 1995){{cn |reason=his twitter says March 29, but does not list a year. I cannot find any other references to his birth date|date=February 2016}}  is an American basketball [[point guard]], most recently for the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball]] team. Felder, who is 5'9" tall, declared for the [[NBA Draft]] at the conclusion of his [[junior (education)|junior]] year. Felder is the [[Horizon League]] career [[assist (basketball)|assist]]s leader.

==High school==
Felder attended [[Pershing High School]] in [[Detroit, Michigan]] where he was named [[Public School League]] MVP his senior season.<ref name="ou bio"/> His senior year, he finished fourth in [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan]] voting.<ref name=nyt_article>{{cite news |title=Key Measure of a 5-9 College Star: 25.3 Points a Game |first=Joanne C. |last=Gerstner |newspaper=New York Times |url=http://mobile.nytimes.com/2016/01/28/sports/ncaabasketball/kahlil-felder-oakland-university.html?_r=0 |date=January 27, 2016 |accessdate=February 11, 2016 }}</ref>

He was not heavily recruited by high-major colleges and was noticed by Oakland assistant coach [[Saddi Washington]].<ref name=nyt_article/> Felder was also recruited by [[Akron Zips men's basketball|Akron]], [[Southern Illinois Salukis men's basketball|Southern Illinois]] and [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2016/02/09/kay-felder-oaklands-big-little-man/80081272/ |title=Kay Felder is Oakland’s big little man |first=Tony |last=Paul |newspaper=Detroit News |date=February 9, 2016 |accessdate=February 12, 2016}}</ref> Oakland offered Felder a scholarship when he was a sophomore and he committed prior to his senior season. To show their commitment to him, Oakland did not recruit a [[point guard]] the season before he arrived so Felder knew there would be no competition.<ref name=espn_article />

==College==
===Freshman season===
Felder won the [[Horizon League]]'s Freshman of the Year Award.<ref name=espn_article />

===Sophomore season===
His sophomore season, Felder finished second in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) with 7.6 assists per game,<ref name="ou bio">{{cite web |url=http://www.goldengrizzlies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/kay_felder_849265.html |title=20 Kay Felder |publisher=Oakland University |accessdate=February 11, 2016}}</ref> two assists behind the leader, [[Jalan West]] of [[Northwestern State Demons basketball|Northwestern State]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/seasons/2015-leaders.html |title=2014-15 Leaders |publisher=Sports Reference LLC |accessdate=February 17, 2016}}</ref> He was also a finalist for the [[Lou Henson Award]], given to the "Mid-Major Player of the Year".<ref name="lute olson press release">{{cite web |url=http://www.luteolsonaward.com/ |archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6eMrKAQ2J |archivedate=January 7, 2016 |date=January 7, 2016 |accessdate=February 11, 2016 |title=Mid-Season Player of Year Honors}}</ref>

===Junior season===
During this season, he was consistently being evaluated as a [[National Basketball Association]] draft prospect, with professional scouts having attended Oakland's games.<ref name=nyt_article/><ref name=espn_article>{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/14704838/oakland-little-man-kay-felder-big-game |title=Kahlil Felder might be only 5-foot-9, but he could do something unprecedented in college basketball |first=Myron |last=Medcalf |date=February 4, 2016 |accessdate=February 12, 2016 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> On December against [[Power Seven Conference]] schools [[2015–16 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]], then-No. 1 [[2015–16 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State Spartans]] and then-No. 5 [[2015–16 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]], Felder averaged 35.0 points, 7.0 assists and made 47.9% of his field goals.<ref>http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kahlil-felder-1/gamelog/2016/</ref> Oakland led at halftime of each of those games, beating Washington, but losing to Michigan State and Virginia. Felder scored 37 points with nine assists against Michigan State in a 99–93 overtime loss at [[The Palace of Auburn Hills]].<ref name=nyt_article/>

Felder was named a top-five finalist for the [[Bob Cousy Award]], given to the top male point guard in Division I.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hoophall.com/news/2016/3/7/final-five-candidates-announced-for-2016-bob-cousy-award.html |title=Final Five Candidates Announced for 2016 Bob Cousy Award |date=March 7, 2016 |accessdate=March 7, 2016 |publisher=Basketball Hall of Fame}}</ref> He was also named the mid-season recipient of the [[Lute Olson Award]], given annually to the most outstanding non-freshman men's college basketball player in [[NCAA Division I]].<ref name="lute olson press release"/> He was placed on the mid-season watch list for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Payne |first1=Terrence |title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced |url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116 |accessdate=February 19, 2016 |work=[[Fox Sports]] |date=February 11, 2016}}</ref>

Felder won the NCAA Player of the Week award on February 9, 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ncaa.com/video/basketball-men/2016-02-09/mbk-mens-basketball-kay-felder-player-week |title=Men's Basketball: Kay Felder named Player of the Week |date=February 9, 2016 |accessdate=February 12, 2016 |publisher=NCAA}}</ref> He also won six Horizon League Player of the Week awards during the season. This tied the Horizon League record.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.wxyz.com/sports/oakland-universitys-kay-felder-named-horizon-league-mens-player-of-the-week-for-6th-time |title=Oakland University's Kay Felder named Horizon League Men's Player of the Week for 6th time |publisher=WXYZ |date=February 15, 2016 |accessdate=February 17, 2016}}</ref>

Despite using only three of his four years of college eligibility, Felder broke the Horizon League career [[assist (basketball)|assist]]s mark of 699, which was originally set by Ralph Lee of [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] in 1986.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2016/02/11/oaklands-felder-sets-horizon-assist-record-loss/80265954/ |title=OU's Felder sets assist record in loss; UDM falls |agency=Associated Press |newspaper=Detroit Free Press |date=February 12, 2016 |accessdate=February 13, 2016}}</ref> Felder also set the Oakland school record for consecutive [[free throw]]s made, making 46 in a row with his last miss on January 29.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/article60543286.html |title=Oakland beats Wright State 89-73 for 2nd place in Horizon |agency=Associated Press |newspaper=The News Tribune |date=February 15, 2016 |accessdate=February 17, 2016}}</ref> Felder was named the [[Horizon League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Horizon League Conference's Player of the Year]] and the All-Horizon League's First Team.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2016/03/01/horizon-league-basketball-kay-felder/81160582/ |title=Horizon League basketball awards: OU's Kay Felder player of the year |first=James |last=Jahnke |newspaper=Detroit Free Press |date=March 1, 2016 |accessdate=March 1, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==
At the conclusion of his junior season, he hired an agent and declared for the [[2016 NBA Draft]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2016/04/05/oaklands-kay-felder-leaving-nba-draft/82648850/ |title=Oakland's Kay Felder declares for NBA draft |first=Mark |last=Snyder |newspaper=Detroit Free Press |date=April 5, 2016 |accessdate=April 5, 2016}}</ref><ref>https://twitter.com/TonyPaul1984/status/718527820138422275</ref> During the 2016 NBA Draft Combine, the 5'9" Felder tied [[Pat Connaughton]] for the second-highest maximum vertical leap recorded in draft combine history at 44".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2016/05/12/kay-felder-nba-draft/84276038/ |title=NBA draft combine: Oakland’s Kay Felder living up to tall ambitions |first=Mark |last=Snyder |newspaper=Detroit Free Press |date=May 13, 2016 |accessdate=May 13, 2016}}</ref> Despite his high marks in the draft combine, Felder is still projected to be a late second round draft pick, with the risk that he'd also not get drafted altogether.
